description:
Interact with a caller-specified page — click, type, scroll, wait — then read it. Use this tool only when the content you need appears after that interaction; for a plain read, use web_access_fetch.

The `actions` run in order in a real browser session that opens on `url`, and the page comes back as it stands after the last one: a site's own search box filled in and submitted, a sort or filter control chosen, a "load more" button, a tab, a cookie banner, rows that render only once scrolled into view.
```json
{ "url": "https://example.com", "actions": [
  { "type": "click", "selector": "input[name=q]" },
  { "type": "write", "text": "standing desk" },
  { "type": "press", "key": "Enter" },
  { "type": "wait", "selector": ".results .item", "timeout": 20000 }
] }
```
The input schema describes each step's fields. Wait on a selector rather than for a fixed time, click a field before `write` types into it, and never begin with a `navigate` to `url` itself.

**Returns:** `body`, the final page (Markdown by default, its HTML with `format: "json"`), with `finalUrl`, `statusCode` and `headers`. If a step fails, the call still succeeds: `error` and `failedActionIndex` (0-based) name the step, and `body` holds the page as it stood then, so read it before fixing that step's selector. With `error` and no `failedActionIndex`, `url` itself did not load and no step ran.

A call holds a browser session for tens of seconds and is billed at the browser rate. Actions can submit forms and change data on the destination, so treat every call as potentially destructive. A browser session is always a GET: it cannot send a POST, PUT or PATCH with a body.

Requests must comply with destination policy, robots directives, rate limits, and access controls.

actions.description: The steps to run, in order, before the page is read: 1 to 50.

all.description: click: click every element matching the selector instead of the first.

key.description: press: the key to press, such as Enter or Tab, or a combination such as Control+A.

milliseconds.description: wait: pause this many milliseconds. Prefer waiting on a selector.

selector.description: CSS selector. Required for click, hover and selectOption; on wait it waits for the element to appear; on scroll it scrolls that element instead of the page.

text.description: write: the text to type into the focused element.

timeout.description: wait with a selector: give up after this many milliseconds.

type.description: What the step does: wait (for a selector to appear, or for a fixed time), click, write (type text into the focused element), press (a key), scroll, navigate (to another URL in the same session, keeping its cookies), hover, or selectOption.

url.description: navigate: the URL to go to, carrying the session's cookies and state.

value.description: selectOption: the option value to select, or an array of them for a multi-select.

countryCode.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, e.g. 'US': get the page as it is served in that country.

format.description: How the final page comes back in body: markdown, the page as clean, LLM-ready text, which suits most reads; or json, the page's HTML as the browser left it.

url.description: The page the browser session opens before the first step, as its full web address.

name: web_access_interact

body.description: The page as the last step left it, or as it stood when a step failed: Markdown with format markdown, its HTML with json.

error.description: Set when a step failed, or when url itself did not load. The call still succeeds, and body holds the page as it stood then.

failedActionIndex.description: 0-based index into actions of the step that failed.

finalUrl.description: The address the session ended on, after any navigation the steps caused.

headers.description: That page's response headers, each name to its values.

statusCode.description: The HTTP status of the page the session ended on.

title: Interact with a web page
